unified-diff.description: A unified patch, either as one text value or as a file manifest whose patch fields Leaf delivers separately on demand.

instructions.producer:
Pipe the exact Git patch, with Git's default `a/` and `b/` prefixes, through this package's producer script into the source:

```bash
git diff <base>...<head> | leaf package run diff patch_manifest.py | leaf data set "$PAGE" <source-id>
```

The script preserves native Git evidence keyed by destination path. It leaves judgment to `lf-diff`: each file’s patch is delivered and checked before its row appears, and textual hunks render when their file opens. A file the widget cannot present shows its refusal and reports it to you as the page's error.

calldiff.description: CallDiff's native JSON diff result, including trees, statuses and optional source coordinates.

instructions.producer:
Pipe CallDiff 0.5.0 or newer with `--format json` directly into the source:

```bash
calldiff diff <base> <head> --entry <entry> --format json | leaf data set "$PAGE" <source-id>
```

Keep the native JSON object intact. Locations are included in the structured trees even without `--locs`.

lf-diff.description: A unified patch with per-file navigation and commentable source lines.
lf-diff.x-instructions: Without `source`, write the exact Git patch in the `<pre>` at column 0, HTML-escaped (& before < and >), or entity text in the patch will change silently. Keep Git's file headers and metadata, and make each hunk's `@@` counts match its lines. Keep the leading space on context lines, and write a context line that is only a space as ` ` so HTML parsing keeps it. With `source`, bind a page-owned patch feed or files manifest and leave the `<pre>` empty. Add `collapsed` to start every file closed. Use view="file" beside a separate file navigator to show one file at a time without a second file listing; datum navigation selects and opens its file. Markdown and plain-text files wrap by default; other files scroll sideways. Set `overflow="wrap"` or `overflow="scroll"` to choose one mode for every file in the widget.
lf-diff.x-example:
diff --git a/feeders/mount.py b/feeders/mount.py
--- a/feeders/mount.py
+++ b/feeders/mount.py
@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@
 def bracket():
-    return "plastic"
+    return "steel"

lf-call-diff.description: A commentable call-tree diff, linked to the `lf-diff` that holds its patch.
lf-call-diff.x-instructions: Set `diff` to the id of the `lf-diff` holding the exact patch. Keep the unchanged items in the tree as landmarks. In a large repository, give each widget one file or entry point. Don't copy the output into markup, add attribute reads as calls, or draw separate before and after diagrams.

lf-worktree-diffs.description: A supplied set of expandable worktree snapshots, with aggregate change totals and independent diff readers.
lf-worktree-diffs.x-instructions: Supply lf-worktree members in review order, with open on the native details of the one to inspect first. The collection totals their supplied file and line counts and lists unavailable snapshots separately. Each member holds ordinary metadata, optional agent commentary, and its own lf-diff. There is no worktree count limit. Read the diff package author instructions for the snapshot contract.
lf-worktree-diffs.x-example:
Preserve a composer draft while switching threads.

diff --git a/draft.js b/draft.js
--- a/draft.js
+++ b/draft.js
@@ -1 +1 @@
-clearDraft();
+saveDraft();

lf-worktree.description: One worktree snapshot and its authored evidence inside lf-worktree-diffs.
lf-worktree.x-instructions: Use label for the worktree name, path for its full filesystem path, branch when attached, and head for the full current commit hash when known. Wrap the evidence in one native details element with a stable id; put open on that details to show it initially. Leaf supplies its summary. Status is changed, clean, or unavailable; known snapshots supply files/additions/deletions from the exact comparison shown by their lf-diff, with optional binary-files included in files but excluded from line totals. Put the commit subject, provenance, and optional agent commentary in ordinary authored markup. Snapshot provenance should identify repository, full HEAD and comparison-base hashes, scope, and capture time. An unavailable row explains the missing evidence in its body and supplies no invented zero totals.
